text:
Keegan Kolesar spent 439 games and a Stanley Cup run in Vegas before landing in Detroit, and his new role is the familiar one: about 10 minutes a night, heavy hitting, little scoring. Through 21 games he has 1 goal, no assists, 6 shots and 52 hits.

The five on five results are the problem. The Red Wings have held only 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about ten points worse than when he sits. That isn't bad luck: the goals have tracked the chances almost exactly. His minutes have slipped to 9.3 over the last ten games.

There is one interesting habit in his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season found 19% of his setups coming from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. The same tracking said his game isn't built on creating offense at five on five.

He scored 17 points for Vegas last season. Our range for him lands well short of that pace now, and the ice time will say whether Detroit sees him as a regular or a fill in.
